A line that starts with three backticks but is not a CommonMark fence opener flips the fence state in the plan parser, so every task heading after it is read as fenced code and silently dropped. `lode doc lint` and `lode doc accept` share the parser, so lint reports nothing and accept mints a truncated task set.

Seen on WL-PLAN-166: Task 4 had a line opening with ```` ```` ```{mermaid} ```` ```` (an inline code span). Accept minted Tasks 1–4 only; Tasks 5–9 appeared after the line was rewrapped so it no longer started with backticks (WL-1368..WL-1372).

Cause: the heading scan in `internal/designdoc/designdoc.go` (around line 355) and `AnnotatePlanTaskHeadings` in `internal/designdoc/plantasks.go` (around line 398) treat any line whose trimmed text starts with ```` ``` ```` or `~~~` as a fence toggle. CommonMark disagrees in two ways: a backtick fence's info string cannot contain a backtick, and a closing fence must use the same character, be at least as long as the opener and carry no info string.

Fix: one fence recogniser in `internal/designdoc` that follows those CommonMark rules, used by every scanner there (`designdoc.go`, `patch.go`, `plantasks.go`).

- [ ] Test: a plan body with a line ```` ```` ```{mermaid} ```` renders ```` followed by two task sections parses all tasks.
- [ ] Test: a four-backtick fence containing a three-backtick line stays one fence.
- [ ] `lode doc lint` on a plan whose `## Tasks` section contains a `### Task N` heading the parser did not count as a task reports it, so a truncated parse is never silent.
